intended_object: The set of elementary transvections of level I, {e_ij(a) = 1 + a·E_ij : i ≠ j, a ∈ I}, for a two-sided ideal I of a ring R, viewed as elements of the elementary subgroup E(n,R). These generate the relative elementary subgroup E(n,I) as a normal subgroup of E(n,R). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `relativeElementarySubgroup`.
explanation:
`elementaryUnit i j hij a` is the unit with matrix `1 + Matrix.single i j a`, which is the elementary transvection e_ij(a). It requires i ≠ j, so it really is a transvection and its inverse is e_ij(-a). The set is exactly {e_ij(a) | i ≠ j, a ∈ I}, packaged as elements of the subgroup `elementarySubgroup ι R`, which is the closure of all such e_ij(c). This is the standard generating set whose normal closure in E(n,R) is E(n,I), and the library takes that normal closure in `relativeElementarySubgroup`.

The generality is the natural one: an arbitrary (not necessarily commutative) ring, a two-sided ideal, and any finite index type with decidable equality. Mathlib has `Matrix.TransvectionStruct` and `Matrix.transvection`, but it has no set or subgroup of transvections with coefficients in an ideal, so there is no more general counterpart. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: for I = ⊥ every generator equals 1, and when the index type has at most one element the set is empty.
